title: Composition
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
if $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ are cohomologically smooth, then
$gf:X\to Z$ is cohomologically smooth, and moreover

$$
\omega_{gf}\;\cong\;\omega_f\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}Lf^*\omega_g.
$$

proof.text: The composite $gf$ is again separated of finite type, so [def-pur-co-smoothness] applies to it: composites of separated, of locally finite type and of quasi-compact morphisms are again such (elementary; Mathlib instances `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated.stableUnderComposition`, `Morphisms/Separated.lean`:71, `locallyOfFiniteType_comp`, `Morphisms/FiniteType.lean`:68, `quasiCompact_comp`, `Morphisms/QuasiCompact.lean`:69). Use [def-pur-co-smoothness] for $f,g$. Their tensor clauses meet [lem-pur-constructible-tensor-composition], giving $c$, $a:W\cong\omega_{gf}$ and $\Phi_K=\theta_{gf,K}(1\otimes a)$, where $W=\omega_f\otimes^LLf^*\omega_g$. Every factor of $\Phi_K$ is invertible. Thus $\theta_{gf,K}$ is invertible for every finite-Tor constructible $K$, and $a^{-1}$ is the asserted dualizing identification.

source.place: Assembly of canonical composition and arbitrary-base-change calculations

proof.text:
Choose two-sided tensor inverses $M_f,M_g$ from clause (1) of [def-pur-co-smoothness]. The objects $\omega_f=Rf^!\Lambda_Y$ and $\omega_g=Rg^!\Lambda_Z$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}$ by the finite-Tor preservation of the constructible exceptional functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and $M_f,M_g\in D^b_{ctf}$ by clause (1). Hence both $W$ and $B=Lf^*M_g\otimes^LM_f$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude, lem-sf-tensor-ctf]. The monoidal comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the inverse identities give
$$W\otimes^LB\cong\omega_f\otimes^LLf^*(\omega_g\otimes^LM_g)\otimes^LM_f\cong\omega_f\otimes^LM_f\cong\Lambda_X,$$
$$B\otimes^LW\cong Lf^*M_g\otimes^L(M_f\otimes^L\omega_f)\otimes^LLf^*\omega_g\cong Lf^*(M_g\otimes^L\omega_g)\cong\Lambda_X.$$
The pullback of the unit is the unit: on constant-coefficient complexes it is inverse image of the constant coefficient sheaf, as specified in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Thus $W$, and hence $\omega_{gf}$ via $a$ from Step 1, is invertible. This proves clause (1).

proof.text: Take arbitrary $t:Z'\to Z$, with $h,s,f',g'$ as in [lem-pur-exceptional-base-change-pasting]. These base-changed vertical maps are separated finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Clause (3) of [def-pur-co-smoothness] gives invertible $\beta_{g,t}$ and $\beta_{f,h}$. Pullback of the two inverse identities for $\omega_g$ is valid by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; hence $Lh^*\omega_g$ is invertible, with its finite-Tor typing supplied by [lem-pur-tensor-mate-base-change]. Apply [lem-pur-tensor-mate-invertible-input] to $(f,\omega_g)$ and $(f',Lh^*\omega_g)$. In the equality of [lem-pur-tensor-mate-base-change], both tensor maps and $1\otimes\beta_{f,h}$ are therefore invertible. It follows that $b_{f,h;\omega_g}$ is invertible. The equality of [lem-pur-exceptional-base-change-pasting] expresses $\beta_{gf,t}$ as the composite of this map, $G_{f'}\beta_{g,t}$ and the two compositors, all invertible. This proves clause (3); Step 2 proves clause (1) and Step 1 proves clause (2), so $gf$ is cohomologically smooth.

lean.statement: theorem cohomologicallySmooth_comp (P : WeilConjectures.PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [Z.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Z ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [QuasiCompact (Z ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [g.IsOver (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g] (hf : IsCohomologicallySmoothCompared P f) (hg : IsCohomologicallySmoothCompared P g) : IsCohomologicallySmoothCompared P (f ≫ g) ∧ Nonempty (@comparedDualizing P X Z (f ≫ g) (P.comparedCompactification (f ≫ g) (Z ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))).hasCompactification ≅ ((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient) X).obj (@comparedDualizing P X Y f (P.comparedCompactification f (Y ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))).hasCompactification)).obj ((L((f)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient])).obj (@comparedDualizing P Y Z g (P.comparedCompactification g (Z ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))).hasCompactification)))
